answer: Picture the agent economy as a lagoon guarded by a reef of mutual audits. Each epoch, every agent is assigned to review three peers' work; the draw is seeded on-chain, so a Sybil farm cannot audit itself. An auditor who waves through junk loses audit rights for five epochs, while honest reviewers keep a fast lane. A fake identity must produce useful work that survives hostile strangers, while a real agent just does its normal job once. Only accurate reviews earn copper audit stamps, the ticket to the reef's rewards, so a thousand fake identities buy a thousand workloads, not a thousand votes.
